title: Unconventional charge density wave order in ErTe$_{3}$: symmetry breakings and fluctuations probed by Raman scattering
authors: Théotime Freitas, Mattia Udina, Alexandr Alekhin, Niloufar Nilforoushan, Sarah Houver, Alain Sacuto, Benito A. Gonzalez, Ian R. Fisher, Indranil Paul, Yann Gallais
abstract: Recent experiments have revealed unexpected mirror-symmetry breakings in the charge density-wave (CDW) state of rare-earth tritellurides, suggesting a putative ferro-axial CDW state. Here we report polarization-resolved Raman scattering measurements tracking the point-group symmetry breakings across the CDW phase transition in the rare-earth tritelluride ErTe$_3$. We show that the mirror-symmetry breakings follow closely the emergence of the CDW order, suggesting a single component CDW order parameter. Furthermore, Raman measurements in the $A_{2g}$ symmetry channel above the CDW transition temperature indicate the absence of significant ferro-axial fluctuations. We discuss the broad implications of these findings with respect to the nature of the CDW state in the tritellurides.
summary: This paper uses polarization-resolved Raman scattering on $	ext{ErTe}_3$ to probe the symmetry breaking associated with its Charge Density Wave (CDW) state. The results indicate that the symmetry breaking is consistent with a single-component CDW order parameter. Furthermore, the measurements rule out the presence of significant ferro-axial fluctuations, refining our understanding of CDW physics in these materials.
main_problem: The study investigates the nature of the Charge Density Wave (CDW) order in rare-earth tritellurides, specifically determining if the symmetry breaking is single-component or multi-component.
main_result: The symmetry breakings observed follow the emergence of the CDW order, strongly suggesting a single-component CDW order parameter, and the measurements rule out significant ferro-axial fluctuations above the transition temperature.
method: Polarization-resolved Raman scattering measurements are used to track point-group symmetry breakings across the CDW phase transition in single crystals.
model_or_system: The physical system is the rare-earth tritelluride $	ext{ErTe}_3$, which is studied as a prototypical weakly correlated 2D CDW material exhibiting structural and electronic instabilities.
key_observables: CDW amplitude mode (AM) intensity and energy, and symmetry-resolved quantities ($\Sigma_{m'}$ and $\Sigma_m$) derived from polarization-dependent Raman responses.
important_parameters: The CDW transition temperature ($T_{	ext{CDW}}$) and the temperature dependence of the Raman response relative to $T_{	ext{CDW}}$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed symmetry breakings are directly linked to the CDW order parameter, though the theoretical description based on simple Peierls-like nesting is noted as potentially deficient.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the temperature dependence of the low-energy Raman response, showing the emergence and polarization dependence of the AM below $T_{	ext{CDW}}$, and quantify symmetry breaking using $\Sigma_{m'}$ and $\Sigma_m$.
paper_structure: The paper analyzes the temperature dependence of the low-energy Raman response, decomposing it by irreducible representations and monitoring symmetry-resolved quantities ($\Sigma_{m'}, \Sigma_m$) to characterize the nature and components of the CDW order parameter.
why_interesting: The detailed symmetry analysis of the CDW state provides insights into the coupling mechanisms between electronic instabilities and lattice distortions, which is relevant to understanding emergent order parameters in strongly correlated systems.
